answer: Operator-Linked Resource Escrow (OLRE). Each new agent identity draws compute, bandwidth, and API quota from a shared resource atlas keyed to the operator's verified payment instrument, not the wallet. Abuse triggers a graduated lock: cooldown, then quota throttling across every identity tied to that instrument. An attacker must acquire and rotate distinct funded instruments per identity, and each lock also forfeits harbor credits already committed to that operator. A crystal audit log records binding evidence, so collateral loss scales with fleet size, not single wallets.
